paths.description: Homepage and news discovery template; tested desktop, mobile, dark/reduced-motion, network, performance, accessibility and crawler rendering.
Representative news article and primary reading journey from homepage; tested desktop, mobile, metadata and no-JS rendering.
España section listing, representing category/index templates.
Latest-news feed, representing a frequently updated listing and repeat-scroll interaction.
Invalid route used to inspect HTTP failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the screenshot remains white and the probe reports colorScheme "normal" and body background rgb(255,255,255).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and supply preference-driven dark tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: A continuously moving market ticker remains active when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found the 45-second cot-marquee animation still running while matchMedia(reduce) was true.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable the marquee under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and expose the same values in a static, scrollable list.

findings.summary: High-contrast and forced-colour adaptation is not defined.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS evidence contains fixed colour tokens and no forced-colors or prefers-contrast adaptation; Lighthouse also found low-contrast consent and LIVE text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast styles, preserve system colours for controls, and avoid suppressing focus outlines.

findings.summary: Navigation changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS or startViewTransition usage despite navigation across MPA templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin article and section navigation with cross-document View Transitions and a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The consent experience can cover the primary content on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a 463x496 modal consent dialog occupying most of its mobile viewport before content interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, plainly worded consent surface with equivalent accept/reject choices and preserve immediate access to editorial content.

findings.summary: Transient overlays are implemented with custom div-based modal infrastructure rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM CSS includes custom tp-modal/tp-backdrop and the consent UI is a div with role=dialog; no native dialog or popover elements were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal consent/account flows and popover for transient menus, retaining declarative dismissal and focus management.

findings.summary: The article template overflows horizontally on a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The article layout primitive measured scrollWidth 373 vs clientWidth 360, a 13px overflow; the homepage was only 1px and latest-news had none.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the fixed-width offender and use min-width:0, max-inline-size:100%, and intrinsic/fluid sizing.

findings.summary: Reusable components rely on viewport rules rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules, while the same header/card system is reused across homepage, section, article and feed layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable card/header regions and use size-aware @container rules where components appear in different slots.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target affordances are insufficient.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on the first link computed to outline:none 0px; Lighthouse reports multiple footer targets only 18-19px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and increase interactive target size/spacing to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44px for primary controls.

findings.summary: Mobile loading and responsiveness are far outside good Core Web Vitals targets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 29.4s, TBT 1,030ms, FCP 4.8s and performance 0.36; the independent trace measured 901ms TBT and a 951ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP resource, defer non-critical scripts/ads, and break the main bundle into schedulable tasks; verify against mobile Lighthouse and field data.

findings.summary: The latest-news mobile template shifts dramatically during load.
findings.evidence: The layout observer measured CLS 0.616 on latest-news, dominated by a 0.604 shift at about 2.45s.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late content and advertising, stabilise font fallbacks, and avoid inserting feed chrome above existing content.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers an excessive resource payload and has a long render-blocking chain.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 335 requests and 12.92MB transferred, including 9.41MB images, 158 scripts and many VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical CSS files, defer non-critical styles/scripts, preload only the confirmed LCP asset, and lazy-load below-fold media and widgets.

findings.summary: Heavy first- and third-party JavaScript dominates main-thread work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 6.0s main-thread work and 3.24s script evaluation; one first-party bundle consumed about 2.03s scripting and 158 scripts were requested.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the large bundle, remove unused/duplicate modules, and load ad, analytics and media integrations only when consent and viewport proximity require them.

findings.summary: Important embedded and image content lacks accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found the football widget iframe without a title; the image audit found 21 images without alt text, and the homepage has no H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every meaningful iframe a concise title, provide appropriate image alt text, and expose one descriptive H1 for the homepage.

findings.summary: Text in the consent interface and live badges fails minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured ratios of 3.21-3.84:1 for consent text/links and 3.44:1 for LIVE badges, below 4.5:1 for the rendered text sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use darker text/link tokens and test all consent and status states to WCAG AA contrast.

findings.summary: Homepage semantics and focus structure contain defects.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no H1; Lighthouse found a UL with a direct DIV child, and the focus probe found no visible outline on the first focusable link.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single meaningful H1, keep list children semantic, and establish a visible logical focus sequence.

findings.summary: The mobile viewport and target sizing constrain inclusive reflow.
findings.evidence: The live probe reports maximum-scale=2.5 and Lighthouse flags many 18-19px-high touch targets; article content also overflows by 13px.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not cap user zoom, remove horizontal overflow, and enlarge target hit areas.

findings.summary: The homepage emits network errors during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED to localhost.sensic.net and a 400 response from an Incapsula resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove production references to localhost, fix or suppress failed vendor calls, and monitor runtime/network errors in production.

findings.summary: Image delivery and document structure contain avoidable defects.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 13 images without dimensions, 23 oversized, 54 without srcset, 33 legacy-format and no modern-format images; Lighthouse found invalid list children.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit dimensions and responsive srcset/sizes, negotiate AVIF/WebP, and correct malformed list structure.

findings.summary: DevTools reports browser-platform hygiene issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices was 0.50 and Inspector Issues recorded cookie-related problems across Dailymotion and TradingView integrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve third-party cookie/inspector warnings, remove stale integrations and ensure production source maps and APIs remain clean.

findings.summary: The advertised sitemap endpoint does not return a sitemap.
findings.evidence: Fetching /sitemap.xml returned a full HTML page rather than XML, while robots.txt is extensive and relies on that indexing surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid XML sitemap with correct content type and reference it from robots.txt; keep canonical/indexing policies consistent.

findings.summary: Cookie security is inconsistent despite strong transport headers.
findings.evidence: Headers include HTTPS, HSTS, CSP, nosniff and framing protection, but cookies reports didomi_token and __adblocker without Secure and sessionActive without HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on every HTTPS cookie, mark session/auth cookies HttpOnly, and use the narrowest workable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The homepage exposes a very large third-party tracking surface.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 48 third-party origins and 12 known trackers; HAR attributes 274 requests and 12.68MB to third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to data minimisation: gate non-essential vendors on consent and need, consolidate analytics, batch events and remove low-value trackers.

findings.summary: Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found both response headers absent, although CSP, HSTS, nosniff and X-Frame-Options were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy for camera, microphone, geolocation and other unused capabilities.

findings.summary: Image assets are disproportionate for a text-led news homepage.
findings.evidence: Images account for 9.41MB; three animated GIFs alone transfer 3.82MB, 1.45MB and 0.92MB, with 23 images oversized and no modern formats detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace GIFs with efficient video/animated image formats, generate responsive AVIF/WebP variants and lazy-load below-fold assets.

findings.summary: Third-party and media work is not proportionate to the initial reading task.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 12.68MB across 274 third-party requests and Lighthouse shows Dailymotion, ad-tech and analytics work before the user requests those surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party/page-weight budget, defer media players and market widgets until visible, and eliminate vendors that do not support the core reading task.

findings.summary: Large ad reservations displace editorial content from the initial viewport.
findings.evidence: Desktop homepage, article and section screenshots reserve roughly 250px-high advertising blocks before primary editorial content; on the article the headline begins below mid-viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce above-the-fold ad height, collapse empty slots promptly and prioritise the article/section heading in the initial viewport.

findings.summary: Main-thread execution blocks interaction for long periods.
findings.evidence: The independent trace recorded a 951ms longest task and 901ms total blocking time; Lighthouse measured 1,030ms TBT and 6.0s main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Break large tasks into schedulable chunks, defer non-critical integrations and isolate expensive work off the main thread where practical.

findings.summary: Background vendor and media work begins before it supports the reading task.
findings.evidence: The initial load issues 274 third-party requests; Lighthouse boot-up attributes work to analytics, consent, Crazy Egg and Dailymotion before a media interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load vendor modules after consent and viewport proximity, batch analytics, and cancel background work when hidden.

findings.summary: The consent wording and blocking presentation undermine freely informed choice.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a near-full mobile dialog whose text says continuing navigation is treated as acceptance, while the primary content is obscured.
findings.suggestedFix: Present equal, explicit accept/reject controls without implied consent from continued browsing, and keep content accessible while preferences are chosen.

findings.summary: CSS is not robust to alternate writing directions.
findings.evidence: The runtime probe confirms lang=es but counts 76 left and 46 right declarations against only four logical-property occurrences.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep lang/dir explicit and migrate layout edges to margin/padding/inset inline/block logical properties.

taskList.title: Cut LCP, scripting and initial payload
Set a third-party privacy and media budget
Repair accessibility semantics, contrast and focus
Respect dark, reduced-motion and contrast preferences
Fix mobile article overflow and component responsiveness
Replace custom modal infrastructure with content-first native primitives
Clean production runtime and inspector errors
